- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean or 0.5–1.0 price point.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is falling, model often overcorrects downward — avoid sharp drops; add 0.5–1.0 price point buffer upward.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots — cap forecast at 1–2 price points below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- Model underestimates mean reversion in volatile periods — if sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price deviates >3σ from 14-day mean, apply mean reversion correction toward historical range.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture sentiment momentum — if sentiment is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0 price point lagged sentiment multiplier to forecast.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “-0.33” (neutral/negative), model tends to overreact — reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% unless confirmed breakout.
